tei:bibl.tei:title: יִגְדַּל (אשכנז)‏
Yigdal, by Daniel ben Yehudah Dayyan (abridged translation by Rev. William Channing Gannett, 1911)
tei:bibl.tei:author: William Channing Gannett
Newton Mann
Max Landsberg
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: This is the abridged rhyming English translation of Yigdal by Rev. William Channing Gannett (1840-1923) made at the request of Rabbi Max Landsberg. Rabbi Landsberg had years earlier requested the same of Gannet’s predecessor, Rev. Newton Mann, at the Unity Church in Rochester, New York in 1884, and Gannet’s version can be considered an update of Mann’s translation. Mann’s translation notably lacked the three final stanzas of Yigdal, possibly at the request of Landsberg in conformance with Reform Jewish theology, but possibly also in order to conform to the ecumenical spirit of collaboration with a Unitarian minister by hewing to agreed principles between Judaism and Unitarianism. Gannet’s update includes translations of 2/3 of these missing stanzas, but also removes two that Mann had translated. In setting Gannett’s translation opposite the Hebrew text, I have retained the Hebrew of the stanzas lacking translation in order to more clearly indicate their absence. Gannet’s translation was first published in his Unity hymns and chorals (1911), pp. 2-3. Gannett’s translation was adopted into the Union Hymnal (1914). Many thanks to Chris Fenner at the Hymnology Archive for researching and informing us of Mann and Gannett’s Yigdal translations. –Aharon Varady
